subject: math
title: Grade 9 Exponent Laws
seo_title: Grade 9 Exponent Laws Worksheets: Free Math Practice with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Exponents and exponent laws with whole-number exponents
meta_desc: Free Grade 9 math worksheets on exponent laws for the BC curriculum: powers with negative and fraction bases, the product law (a³ × a⁴ = a⁷), the quotient law, the power of a power, the zero exponent, and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Multiply powers with the same base: add the exponents. Divide: subtract them. Power of a power: multiply them.
key_sub: a³ × a⁴ = a⁷ (not a¹²), a⁷ ÷ a³ = a⁴, (a³)⁴ = a¹², and a⁰ = 1 (not 0) for any a ≠ 0.
body_html:
Powers

A power is a short way to write repeated multiplication. In a4, a is the base and 4 is the exponent: a4 = a × a × a × a. Watch the brackets: in (−2)4 the base is −2, but in −24 the base is 2.

Negative bases

Evaluate (−2)4 and −24.

(−2)4 = (−2) × (−2) × (−2) × (−2) = 16. −24 = −(2 × 2 × 2 × 2) = −16.

Answer: 16 and −16

Product law

When you multiply powers with the same base, keep the base and add the exponents: am × an = am+n.

Product law

Simplify 2x3 × 4x5.

Multiply the coefficients: 2 × 4 = 8. Add the exponents: 3 + 5 = 8.

Answer: 8x8

Quotient law

When you divide powers with the same base, keep the base and subtract the exponents: am ÷ an = am−n.

Quotient law

Simplify 12x7 ÷ 4x2.

Divide the coefficients: 12 ÷ 4 = 3. Subtract the exponents: 7 − 2 = 5.

Answer: 3x5

Power of a power

For a power raised to a power, multiply the exponents: (am)n = amn. An exponent outside brackets applies to every factor inside: (ab)n = anbn.

Power of a power

Simplify (2a3)4.

(2a3)4 = 2a3 × 2a3 × 2a3 × 2a3. Raise each factor: 24 = 16 and (a3)4 = a12.

Answer: 16a12

Zero exponent

Any non-zero number to the power 0 is 1. Each step down the table divides by 2, so 20 = 2 ÷ 2 = 1. The quotient law agrees: a3 ÷ a3 = a0, and anything divided by itself is 1.

faq.q: What exponent laws are in Grade 9 math in BC?
faq.a: Mathematics 9 in BC covers exponents and exponent laws with whole-number exponents: the product law aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ, the quotient law aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ, the power of a power (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ, the power of a product (ab)ⁿ = aⁿbⁿ, and the zero exponent a⁰ = 1.

faq.q: Why is a³ × a⁴ = a⁷ and not a¹²?
faq.a: a³ is 3 factors of a and a⁴ is 4 more, so together there are 3 + 4 = 7 factors. You add the exponents when you multiply powers; you multiply them only for a power of a power, like (a³)⁴ = a¹².

faq.q: Why is any number to the power of zero equal to 1?
faq.a: Look at the pattern 2³ = 8, 2² = 4, 2¹ = 2: each step divides by 2, so 2⁰ = 1. The quotient law also gives a³ ÷ a³ = a⁰, and any non-zero number divided by itself is 1.

faq.q: What is the difference between (−2)⁴ and −2⁴?
faq.a: In (−2)⁴ the base is −2, so (−2)⁴ = 16. In −2⁴ the base is 2 and the negative sign is applied after, so −2⁴ = −16.

items.q: In 7<sup>4</sup>, which number is the base?
items.e: The base is the number that is multiplied: 7. The small raised 4 is the exponent. 7<sup>4</sup> = 7 × 7 × 7 × 7 = 2401 is the value of the power.
5 is used as a factor 4 times, so the base is 5 and the exponent is 4: 5<sup>4</sup>. Count the factors (4), not the × signs (3).
3<sup>4</sup> = 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 81. Not 12: that is 3 × 4. Not 64: that is 4<sup>3</sup>. Not 27: that uses only three 3s.
10<sup>5</sup> is a 1 followed by 5 zeros: 100 000. Not 50: that is 10 × 5.
x is used as a factor 5 times: x5. 5x means x + x + x + x + x, which is repeated addition, not repeated multiplication.
The exponent 3 tells you to use the base a as a factor 3 times: a3 = a × a × a. It is not 3a, which is 3 × a.
The brackets make −2 the base: (−2) × (−2) × (−2) × (−2) = 16. An even number of negative factors gives a positive answer.
With no brackets the base is 2, not −2: −2<sup>4</sup> = −(2 × 2 × 2 × 2) = −16. Compare (−2)<sup>4</sup> = 16.
2<sup>5</sup> = 32 and 5<sup>2</sup> = 25, so 2<sup>5</sup> is greater. Swapping the base and the exponent changes the value.
(−3) × (−3) × (−3): (−3) × (−3) = 9, then 9 × (−3) = −27. An odd number of negative factors gives a negative answer. Not −9: that is (−3) × 3.
Eight factors of −1: every pair multiplies to 1, so (−1)<sup>8</sup> = 1. Not −8: that is (−1) × 8.
0.5<sup>2</sup> = 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.25. Not 1: that is 0.5 × 2. Count the decimal places: 1 + 1 = 2 places.

items.q: Which power has a negative value?
items.e: (−5)<sup>3</sup> = −125 has an odd number of negative factors. (−5)<sup>2</sup> = 25 and (−5)<sup>4</sup> = 625 have an even number, and 5<sup>3</sup> = 125 has no negative factors.
The factor −6 is used 3 times, so the base is −6 in brackets and the exponent is 3: (−6)<sup>3</sup> = −216. −6 × 3 = −18 is not repeated multiplication.
(−0.3) × (−0.3) = 0.09. Two negative factors give a positive answer, and 3 × 3 = 9 with 2 decimal places. Not −0.6: that is (−0.3) × 2.
Cube the numerator and the denominator: 23 × 23 × 23 = 827. Not 69: that multiplies by 3 instead of cubing. Not 83: cube the denominator too.
Powers come before multiplication: 2<sup>4</sup> = 16, then 3 × 16 = 48. Not 1296: that is (3 × 2)<sup>4</sup>. Not 24: that is 3 × 2 × 4. Not 96: that uses 2<sup>5</sup> = 32.
(−2)<sup>3</sup> = (−2) × (−2) × (−2) = −8. Put a negative value in brackets before you raise it to a power. Not −6: that is (−2) × 3.
Only a is squared: 2 × 32 = 2 × 9 = 18. Not 36: that is (2 × 3)2. Not 12: that is 2 × 3 × 2.

items.q: The picture shows 23 × 24 as factors. Which single power is it equal to?
items.e: Count all the factors of 2: 3 + 4 = 7, so 2<sup>3</sup> × 2<sup>4</sup> = 2<sup>7</sup>. Keep the base. Not 2<sup>12</sup>: do not multiply the exponents. Not 4<sup>7</sup>: do not multiply the bases.
Same base, so add the exponents: 2 + 4 = 6. 5<sup>2</sup> × 5<sup>4</sup> = 5<sup>6</sup>. The base stays 5.
x3 × x4 = (x × x × x) × (x × x × x × x) = x7. Add the exponents: 3 + 4 = 7. Multiplying them (3 × 4 = 12) is the most common mistake.
Keep the base 3 and add the exponents: 4 + 5 = 9. 3<sup>4</sup> × 3<sup>5</sup> = 3<sup>9</sup>.
a on its own means a1. So add 1 + 5 = 6: a × a5 = a6. Not a5: the a on its own still counts as one factor.
The base is −2 in both powers, so add the exponents: 3 + 2 = 5. (−2)<sup>5</sup> = −32.

items.q: 7<sup>2</sup> × 7<sup>☐</sup> = 7<sup>8</sup>. Which exponent goes in the box?
items.e: The exponents add: 2 + ☐ = 8, so ☐ = 6. Check: 7<sup>2</sup> × 7<sup>6</sup> = 7<sup>8</sup>. Not 4: 2 × 4 = 8 multiplies the exponents.
Add all the exponents: 4 + 2 + 3 = 9. y4 × y2 × y3 = y9. Not y24: that multiplies them.
The bases are different, so the product law does not apply. Evaluate each power: 2<sup>3</sup> = 8 and 3<sup>2</sup> = 9, then 8 × 9 = 72.

items.q: Simplify (12)2 × (12)3.
items.e: The base is 12 in both powers, so add the exponents: 2 + 3 = 5. (12)5 = 132.

4 + 6 = 10, so 2<sup>4</sup> × 2<sup>6</sup> = 2<sup>10</sup>. 2<sup>2</sup> × 2<sup>5</sup> = 2<sup>7</sup> (2 × 5 = 10 is the multiplying mistake). 2<sup>5</sup> + 2<sup>5</sup> = 2 × 2<sup>5</sup> = 2<sup>6</sup>: adding powers is not the same as multiplying them.
Add the exponents in each product: 4 + 4 = 8, 2 + 6 = 8, 1 + 7 = 8, but 2 + 4 = 6. So x2 × x4 = x6, not x8. (2 × 4 = 8 is the multiplying mistake.)
Multiply the coefficients and add the exponents: 2 × 4 = 8 and 3 + 5 = 8. So the answer is 8x8. Not 6x8: do not add the coefficients.
Coefficients: (−3) × 5 = −15. Exponents: 2 + 4 = 6. So the answer is −15m6. Not −15m8: that multiplies the exponents.

items.q: x☐ × x4 × x = x10. Which exponent goes in the box?
items.e: x means x1, so ☐ + 4 + 1 = 10 and ☐ = 5. Not 6: that forgets the exponent 1 on x.
Work with each base on its own. a: 2 + 4 = 6. b: 3 + 1 = 4 (b means b1). So the answer is a6b4.
Coefficients: 4 × 3 = 12 (the middle factor has coefficient 1). Exponents: 2 + 3 + 1 = 6. So the answer is 12n6.
Coefficients: (−2) × 3 = −6. a: 3 + 1 = 4. b: 1 + 4 = 5. So the answer is −6a4b5. Not −6a3b4: a and b on their own have exponent 1, not 0.

items.q: Write 8 × 2<sup>5</sup> as a single power of 2.
items.e: First write 8 as a power of 2: 8 = 2<sup>3</sup>. Then 2<sup>3</sup> × 2<sup>5</sup> = 2<sup>8</sup> = 256. Not 16<sup>5</sup>: do not multiply 8 × 2. Not 2<sup>6</sup>: 8 is three factors of 2, not one.

items.q: The picture shows 36 ÷ 32. Each crossed-out pair of 3s divides to 1. Which power is left?
items.e: 6 factors on top, 2 on the bottom. Each pair cancels, so 6 − 2 = 4 factors are left: 3<sup>6</sup> ÷ 3<sup>2</sup> = 3<sup>4</sup>. Not 3<sup>3</sup>: do not divide the exponents (6 ÷ 2 = 3).
Same base, so subtract the exponents: 6 − 2 = 4. 5<sup>6</sup> ÷ 5<sup>2</sup> = 5<sup>4</sup>. Not 1<sup>4</sup>: keep the base, do not divide 5 ÷ 5.
Subtract the exponents: 9 − 3 = 6. x9 ÷ x3 = x6. Not x3: that divides 9 ÷ 3.
10 − 5 = 5, so 2<sup>10</sup> ÷ 2<sup>5</sup> = 2<sup>5</sup> = 32. Not 2<sup>2</sup>: 10 ÷ 5 = 2 divides the exponents.
a means a1, so subtract 1: 8 − 1 = 7. a8 ÷ a = a7.
A fraction bar means divide. Subtract the exponents: 8 − 2 = 6, so the answer is y6. Not y4: that divides 8 ÷ 2.
7<sup>5</sup> ÷ 7<sup>3</sup> = 7<sup>2</sup> = 49. Not 14: that is 7 × 2. Not 1: that divides the bases 7 ÷ 7.
10<sup>8</sup> ÷ 10<sup>5</sup> = 10<sup>3</sup> = 1000. Not 30: that is 10 × 3. Not 1: keep the base 10.
Keep the base −4 and subtract: 7 − 4 = 3. (−4)<sup>3</sup> = −64. Not 4<sup>3</sup> = 64: the base is still negative.

items.q: 6<sup>☐</sup> ÷ 6<sup>3</sup> = 6<sup>5</sup>. Which exponent goes in the box?
items.e: The exponents subtract: ☐ − 3 = 5, so ☐ = 8. Check: 6<sup>8</sup> ÷ 6<sup>3</sup> = 6<sup>5</sup>. Not 2: that subtracts 5 − 3. Not 15: that multiplies 5 × 3.

12 − 8 = 4, so 3<sup>12</sup> ÷ 3<sup>8</sup> = 3<sup>4</sup>. 3<sup>12</sup> ÷ 3<sup>3</sup> = 3<sup>9</sup> (12 ÷ 3 = 4 is the dividing mistake). 3<sup>8</sup> ÷ 3<sup>2</sup> = 3<sup>6</sup> and 9<sup>8</sup> ÷ 9<sup>4</sup> = 9<sup>4</sup>.

items.q: Simplify (23)5 ÷ (23)2.
items.e: Same base 23, so subtract the exponents: 5 − 2 = 3. The answer is (23)3 = 827.
Divide the coefficients: 12 ÷ 4 = 3. Subtract the exponents: 7 − 2 = 5. So the answer is 3x5. Not 8x5: do not subtract 12 − 4.
(−20) ÷ 5 = −4 and 6 − 3 = 3, so the answer is −4a3. Not −4a2: that divides 6 ÷ 3.
Work with each base. a: 5 − 2 = 3. b: 6 − 1 = 5 (b means b1). So the answer is a3b5.
Work left to right: x4 × x6 = x10 (add), then x10 ÷ x3 = x7 (subtract). Not x21: that multiplies 4 × 6 first. Not x13: that adds all three exponents.
Top: 5<sup>4</sup> × 5<sup>3</sup> = 5<sup>7</sup>. Then 5<sup>7</sup> ÷ 5<sup>5</sup> = 5<sup>2</sup> = 25. Not 78 125: that is 5<sup>12</sup> ÷ 5<sup>5</sup> = 5<sup>7</sup>. Not 10: that is 5 × 2.
9 − 6 = 3, so the answer is (−3)<sup>3</sup> = −27. Three negative factors give a negative answer. Not −9: that is (−3) × 3.
18 ÷ 6 = 3. m: 8 − 2 = 6. n: n5 ÷ n5 = 1, so no n is left. So the answer is 3m6. Not 3m4: that divides 8 ÷ 2.

items.q: 48y☐ ÷ 8y3 = 6y4. Which exponent goes in the box?
items.e: 48 ÷ 8 = 6 checks the coefficient. For the exponents: ☐ − 3 = 4, so ☐ = 7. Not 1: that is 4 − 3. Not 12: that is 4 × 3.

sets.title: Power of a power, product and quotient

items.e: (2<sup>3</sup>)<sup>2</sup> = 2<sup>3</sup> × 2<sup>3</sup> = 2<sup>6</sup>. Multiply the exponents: 3 × 2 = 6. Not 2<sup>5</sup>: do not add them. Not 2<sup>9</sup>: that uses 3<sup>2</sup> = 9 as the exponent.
The outside exponent 3 says to use x4 as a factor 3 times: x4 × x4 × x4 = x12. It is not 3x4, which is x4 + x4 + x4.
Multiply the exponents: 5 × 2 = 10. (a5)2 = a5 × a5 = a10. Not a7: that adds 5 + 2.
2 × 4 = 8, so (5<sup>2</sup>)<sup>4</sup> = 5<sup>8</sup>. Not 10<sup>4</sup>: 5<sup>2</sup> is 25, not 10. Not 5<sup>16</sup>: that uses 2<sup>4</sup> = 16 as the exponent.
3 × 5 = 15, so (y3)5 = y15. Not y8: that adds. Not y243: that is 35 in the exponent.
(2<sup>2</sup>)<sup>3</sup> = 2<sup>6</sup> = 64. You can also work inside first: 2<sup>2</sup> = 4 and 4<sup>3</sup> = 64. Not 32: that is 2<sup>5</sup>. Not 12: that is 4 × 3.
2 × 3 = 6, so (10<sup>2</sup>)<sup>3</sup> = 10<sup>6</sup> = 1 000 000. Not 100 000: that is 10<sup>5</sup> (adding). Not 100 000 000: that is 10<sup>8</sup>, because 2<sup>3</sup> = 8.

items.q: (7<sup>☐</sup>)<sup>4</sup> = 7<sup>20</sup>. Which exponent goes in the box?
items.e: The exponents multiply: ☐ × 4 = 20, so ☐ = 5. Check: (7<sup>5</sup>)<sup>4</sup> = 7<sup>20</sup>. Not 16: that is 20 − 4, as if the exponents were added.
4 = 2<sup>2</sup>, so 4<sup>5</sup> = (2<sup>2</sup>)<sup>5</sup> = 2<sup>10</sup>. Not 2<sup>7</sup>: that adds 2 + 5. Not 8<sup>5</sup>: 4 is not 8.
3 × 4 = 12, so (2<sup>3</sup>)<sup>4</sup> = 2<sup>12</sup>. The others add to 12 but multiply to 32, 36 and 27.
(2x)3 = 2x × 2x × 2x. Every factor inside the brackets is cubed: 23x3 = 8x3. Not 2x3: the 2 must be cubed too. Not 6x3: 23 is 8, not 2 × 3.
Square the 3 and the a2: 32 = 9 and (a2)2 = a4. So the answer is 9a4. Not 6a4: 32 is 9, not 3 × 2.
(−2)2 = 4 (two negative factors) and (y3)2 = y6. So the answer is 4y6. Not 4y5: multiply 3 × 2, do not add.
(−2)3 = −8 (three negative factors) and (y3)3 = y9. So the answer is −8y9.
Square the top and the bottom: (25)2 = 2252 = 425. Not 410: that multiplies by 2 instead of squaring.
The exponent applies to the top and the bottom: (xy)3 = xy × xy × xy = x3y3.
Raise each factor: (a2)4 = a8 and (b3)4 = b12. So the answer is a8b12. Not a6b7: that adds 4 to each exponent.
Power of a power first: (x3)2 = x6. Then the product law: x6 × x4 = x10. Not x9: that adds all three. Not x13: that uses 32 = 9.
Raise every factor to the 4th power: 24 = 16, (a3)4 = a12 and b4. So the answer is 16a12b4. Not 8a12b4: 24 is 16, not 2 × 4.

Top: (m2n3)3 = m6n9. Divide: m: 6 − 4 = 2, n: 9 − 5 = 4. So the answer is m2n4. Not mn: that adds 3 to each exponent inside instead of multiplying. Not m10n14: that adds the bottom exponents instead of subtracting.

sets.title: Zero exponent, mixed practice and word problems

items.e: Any non-zero number to the power 0 is 1, so 7<sup>0</sup> = 1. It is not 0: 7<sup>0</sup> = 7<sup>2</sup> ÷ 7<sup>2</sup> = 49 ÷ 49 = 1.
A number divided by itself is 1. With the quotient law: x5 ÷ x5 = x0, and x0 = 1. So x0 is 1, not 0.
The base is −5 (in brackets), and any non-zero base to the power 0 is 1.
With no brackets the base is 5: −5<sup>0</sup> = −(5<sup>0</sup>) = −1. Compare (−5)<sup>0</sup> = 1.
Only x has the exponent 0: 4x0 = 4 × 1 = 4. Not 1: the 4 is not raised to the power 0.
Now the brackets make 4x the base, and any non-zero base to the power 0 is 1. Compare 4x0 = 4.
20 = 1 and 30 = 1, so the sum is 1 + 1 = 2. Not 0: that uses a0 = 0. Not 5: that uses a0 = a.

2<sup>3</sup> × 2<sup>4</sup> = 2<sup>7</sup>, then 2<sup>7</sup> ÷ 2<sup>5</sup> = 2<sup>2</sup> = 4. Not 128: that is 2<sup>12</sup> ÷ 2<sup>5</sup> = 2<sup>7</sup>. Not 32: that stops at 2<sup>5</sup>.
(x4)2 = x8, then x8 ÷ x6 = x2. Not 1: that adds 4 + 2 = 6 and gets x0. Not x14: that adds instead of subtracting.
Coefficients: 3 × 2 = 6. Exponents: 4 + 3 − 7 = 0, and x0 = 1. So the answer is 6 × 1 = 6. Not 0 and not 6x: x0 is 1.
(a2b)3 = a6b3. Then a6 ÷ a6 = a0 = 1, so b3 is left. Not ab3: a0 is 1, not a. Not b: the b is cubed too.

(2<sup>3</sup>)<sup>2</sup> = 2<sup>6</sup>, 2<sup>6</sup> ÷ 2<sup>4</sup> = 2<sup>2</sup> = 4, and 5<sup>0</sup> = 1. So 4 + 1 = 5. Not 4: that uses 5<sup>0</sup> = 0. Not 9: that uses 5<sup>0</sup> = 5. Not 3: that adds the exponents, (2<sup>3</sup>)<sup>2</sup> = 2<sup>5</sup>.

items.q: In a science class in Burnaby, a sample of bacteria doubles every hour. After 3 hours it is 2<sup>3</sup> times its first size. After 5 more hours, how many times its first size is it?
items.e: It doubles 3 times, then 5 more times: 2<sup>3</sup> × 2<sup>5</sup> = 2<sup>8</sup> = 256. Not 32 768: that is 2<sup>15</sup> (multiplying the exponents). Not 16: that is 2 × 8.

items.q: Ji-woo’s tablet has 2<sup>8</sup> GB of storage. Each movie he downloads uses 2<sup>2</sup> GB. How many movies fit on the tablet?
items.e: 2<sup>8</sup> ÷ 2<sup>2</sup> = 2<sup>6</sup> = 64 movies. Not 16: that is 2<sup>4</sup> (8 ÷ 2 divides the exponents). Not 6: that is only the exponent.

items.q: A square plot in a Kelowna community garden has sides of 5x3 m. Which expression gives its area in square metres?
items.e: Area = side × side = (5x3)2 = 52 × (x3)2 = 25x6. Not 5x6: square the 5 too. Not 20x3: that is the perimeter, 4 × 5x3.

items.q: Leah builds a planter box shaped like a cube with edges of 2x2 cm. Which expression gives its volume in cubic centimetres?
items.e: Volume = edge × edge × edge = (2x2)3 = 23 × (x2)3 = 8x6. Not 6x6: 23 is 8, not 2 × 3. Not 8x5: multiply the exponents 2 × 3, do not add.

items.q: A rectangular garden bed at a Surrey school is 4x3 m long and 3x2 m wide. Which expression gives its area in square metres?
items.e: Area = length × width = 4x3 × 3x2. Multiply the coefficients (4 × 3 = 12) and add the exponents (3 + 2 = 5): 12x5. Not 7x5: do not add 4 + 3.

items.q: A salmon hatchery on Vancouver Island has 10<sup>6</sup> eggs. It splits them equally into 10<sup>2</sup> trays. How many eggs go in each tray?
items.e: 10<sup>6</sup> ÷ 10<sup>2</sup> = 10<sup>4</sup> = 10 000 eggs per tray. Subtract the exponents: 6 − 2 = 4. Not 10<sup>3</sup>: that divides 6 ÷ 2.

items.q: The number of cells in a sample is 300 × 2t, where t is the time in hours. How many cells are there at the start, when t = 0?
items.e: At t = 0 the number is 300 × 20 = 300 × 1 = 300. Not 0: 20 is 1, not 0. Not 600: 20 is not 2. Not 1: 20 = 1 is only the factor; multiply it by 300.

items.q: A recycling bin at a Victoria school is a cube with edges of 10<sup>2</sup> cm. How many small cubes with edges of 10 cm would fill it?
items.e: Volume of the bin: (10<sup>2</sup>)<sup>3</sup> = 10<sup>6</sup> cm³. Volume of a small cube: 10<sup>3</sup> cm³. 10<sup>6</sup> ÷ 10<sup>3</sup> = 10<sup>3</sup> = 1000. Not 1 000 000: that forgets to divide by the small cube’s volume.
